# RETRO: t1 / PR #12439

## What worked

- Naming the dependency (Hyprland at Omarchy's target version) in the brief led both reviewers to read v0.56.2 source; that settled the decisive `hl.monitor` rule-copy and `currentFormat` questions without a desktop.
- Opus's cited-semantics `hyprctl` model with labelled positive-control variants turned source facts into concrete consequences; a flock wrapper made the restore race deterministic.
- Cross-examination was productive: each single-source claim was confirmed by the other reviewer, and Sol refined the race impact (a revert is possible today in some profile combinations).

## Friction and process deviations

- Opus reviewer (self-reported in `opus/RETRO.md`): one host `jq` read of intake JSON, one owner-resolving `ls -la` on its own fixture directories, one diff extract briefly written to the session scratchpad then moved into `opus/notes/`, one host `bash -n` on its own stubs (repeated inside `review.py`). No PR code ran outside the sandbox and no host state changed. Public claims do not depend on those outputs.
- `node` is absent from the `review.py` sandbox, so Node-based `monitor-test.sh` could not run. Possible toolkit feature request: optional node in the sandbox tool set.
- Sol's first report was short (26 lines) but substantive; length alone was not a quality signal.

## Carry forward

- Keep asking reviewers to identify the dependency version from the repository/package build.
- Brief should remind reviewers that the session scratchpad is outside the allowed write area.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Two Hyprland 0.56.2 API assumptions in `bin/omarchy-monitor-profile` break core profile switching, recovery and rollback: re-enabling outputs and saving the video mode. Both fixes look small. The test stub models the opposite of both behaviors, so the PR's suite passes. Lid handling, a restore race and mirrored layouts need further changes.

**Verified** at head `45fcf3d`:

- Applying a profile with a disconnected connector changes nothing.
- Targets are staged beyond both layouts' bounds before sources are disabled.
- DPMS-only differences do not trigger a restore or wake.
- Profile names are validated (`../bad` is refused), and monitor names reach Lua only through `jq @json`.
- The Lua dispatchers used (`hl.dsp.dpms`, `hl.dsp.workspace.move`, `hl.dsp.focus`) exist in Hyprland 0.56.2 with the shapes the script uses.
- The watcher behaves as before when no profile is active.
- In an isolated sandbox, `monitor-profile-test.sh` (14/14), `monitor-state-test.sh`, `monitor-recovery-test.sh` and `monitor-modeless-test.sh` pass.

### A profile cannot re-enable an output that was disabled

`configure_monitor` sends `hl.monitor({ output, mode, position, scale, transform [, mirror] })` and never `disabled = false`. In Hyprland 0.56.2, `hl.monitor` starts from the existing rule with the same output name and changes only the fields given (`src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsConfigRules.cpp`, the `existing` rule copy). `CMonitorRuleManager::add` then replaces that rule, and a rule with `m_disabled` keeps the output off. Once `disable_monitor` has run for an output, every later enabling call for it inherits `disabled = true` until a config reload. The same applies to the clamshell and manual-disable toggles, which are also named `disabled = true` rules. A `mirror` set by the mirror toggle is inherited the same way.

```text
apply external   -> hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", disabled = true })
apply desk       -> hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", mode = ..., position = ... })
                    rule copied from "eDP-1" still has disabled = true
                 -> "Cannot apply desk: eDP-1 did not activate", rollback
```

Results from a stub `hyprctl` that models the cited Hyprland rule semantics, with the PR script unmodified (not a real compositor run):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `external` active, then `apply desk` | exits 1, `eDP-1 did not activate` |
| `external` active, external display unplugged, `restore` | exits 1, no physical output enabled (Hyprland's headless fallback only) |
| Failed switch from `desk` rolled back | panel stays off, active name still `desk`, while the notice says the previous layout was restored |

A diagnostic copy of the script that adds `disabled = false` (together with the mode fix below) passes all three scenarios in the same model.

**Impact:** Switching from an external-only profile back to a layout that includes the laptop panel fails until Hyprland reloads its config. Undocking with an external-only profile active can leave no usable screen, which the new manual text says cannot happen. Rollback cannot restore an output that the failed switch disabled.

**Suggested change:** Send `disabled = false` in every enabling `hl.monitor` call (apply, staging, rollback and fallback recovery). Also send `mirror` explicitly (empty or the intended source) so an inherited mirror does not persist.

### The saved `mode` is the pixel format, not a video mode

`save_profile`, `restore_layout_json` and `recover_usable_output` use `.currentFormat` as the mode. In Hyprland 0.56.2, `currentFormat` comes from `formatToString(drmFormat)` in `src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp`, so it holds values such as `XRGB8888`. It is always a non-null string, so the `WxH@R` fallback in the jq expression never runs. `CMonitorRuleParser::parseMode` rejects a mode without `x`, and the output falls back to its preferred mode. The eval error is discarded (`>/dev/null 2>&1`).

**Impact:** Nothing visible changes on outputs using Omarchy's default `mode = "preferred"`. An output saved at a non-preferred resolution or refresh rate, such as the `2560x1440@144` example in `config/hypr/monitors.lua`, never matches its profile, so every apply ends in "did not settle" and rollback. In the stub model, a DP-1 profile saved at 143.973 Hz fails and ends at 59.951 Hz. The diagnostic copy settles at 143.973 Hz.

**Suggested change:** Build the mode from `width`, `height` and `refreshRate` (the expression already used as the fallback) and stop reading `currentFormat`.

### Lid close, wake and login clamshell handling still conflict with an active profile

The watcher now skips `sync_clamshell` and the docked-laptop poll while a profile is active. Other paths still call `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` directly: `bin/omarchy-system-lid-close`, `bin/omarchy-system-wake` and the lid-switch binding in `default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua`. When the lid closes with an external display active, the clamshell script writes a persistent `disabled = true` rule for the internal panel and reloads Hyprland, whether or not a profile is active.

- **Lid close with a profile that includes the panel.** In the stub model, the watcher reacted with 8 restore attempts and 8 "Monitor profile failed" notices. The panel stays off only because of the re-enable issue above. With that issue fixed, the profile turns the panel back on under the closed lid.
- **Login.** Only the watcher's startup sync ran clamshell reconciliation at login, and it is now skipped. In the stub model, a login with the lid open, undocked, after a docked lid-closed session, left no physical output enabled with the PR watcher. The base watcher recovered the panel. This assumes no lid event is replayed at startup, which was not checked.

**Impact:** The PR description's "without fighting clamshell handling" holds only for the watcher's own clamshell call. Lid events and the clamshell flag still override, or fight with, the selected profile.

**Suggested change:** Decide what a profile that includes the internal panel should do when the lid closes. Then either make the clamshell entry points consult the active profile, or make profile restore treat a closed lid as removing the panel. Keep the startup stale-flag cleanup running while a profile is active.

### `restore` reads the active profile before taking the lock

`restore` reads `name=$(active_profile)` before `apply_profile` takes `flock`. A user `apply B` writes the new name only at the end. The outputs it enables or disables emit `monitoradded`/`monitorremoved` mid-apply, and the watcher immediately runs `restore`, which can capture the previous name A. After B releases the lock, `restore` applies A and records A as active again.

**Impact:** Depending on which outputs the two profiles use, the stale restore either undoes the user's switch (when the old profile needs only outputs that are still enabled) or shows a false "Monitor profile failed" notice right after a successful switch. A deterministic lock-parking run in the stub model shows the false notice with the PR as is, and a silent revert once re-enabling is fixed. The exact real-time interleaving was not observed on a compositor.

**Suggested change:** Resolve the active profile name inside the locked section, and keep the fallback recovery under the same lock.

### Saving a mirrored layout creates a profile the tool rejects

Hyprland 0.56.2 reports `mirrorOf` as the source monitor's numeric ID. `save` stores it verbatim (for example `mirror: "0"`), while `validate_profile` requires `mirror` to be one of the profile's output names. In the stub model, `save` reports success and marks the profile active. `list` then omits it, `current` prints nothing, and `apply` exits with `Invalid monitor profile`.

**Impact:** A mirrored presentation layout appears to save successfully but cannot be listed, shown as current, applied or restored.

**Suggested change:** Map the ID to the output name when saving and compare by name when matching. Alternatively, refuse to save mirrored layouts.

### Smaller issues

- **Notification bursts:** `quiet=true` suppresses only the success notice. Each output change emits both v1 and v2 events, and the watcher runs `restore` four times per event (immediately and after 1, 3 and 7 seconds), so up to 8 attempts per output. In the stub model, one undock with `desk` active produced 8 identical "Monitor profile unavailable" notices.
- **`save` also activates the profile:** `save_profile` writes the active name. The new manual says applying a profile is what makes it persist. Saving `presentation` while `desk` is active silently switches the profile used for reconnect restore.
- **Applying a layout that already matches does not refocus the saved primary output:** the early return in `apply_profile_locked` records the name and exits before `hl.dsp.focus`. `profile_matches` does not compare focus. Refocusing and notifying there only when `quiet` is not `true` keeps the idle `restore` path a no-op.

**Optional test improvement:** The `hyprctl` stub in `monitor-profile-test.sh` reports `currentFormat` as `"1920x1080@60.00Hz"` and marks an output enabled on any `hl.monitor` call without `disabled = true`. Hyprland 0.56.2 does neither, which is why the suite passes with both main issues present. Real field shapes (`currentFormat: "XRGB8888"`, numeric `mirrorOf`) and a stub that keeps per-output rule fields would have caught them.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR head against Hyprland v0.56.2 and Quickshell v0.3.1 source. The PR's shell tests ran in an isolated sandbox with `hyprctl` stubbed. `monitor-test.sh` did not run because Node was unavailable in the sandbox. Behavior scenarios used a stub `hyprctl` that encodes only the cited Hyprland semantics, with labelled diagnostic copies as positive controls. These are not real compositor or hardware runs. The Display panel was not checked visually, and DPMS behavior on real monitors was not tested. The changed files are unchanged on the current tip of the PR's base branch.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks of single-source claims, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
